It's also extremely expensive to live here, and wages don't keep up. I moved downtown in October 2016 for $1600/mo. I had to move because my rent went up to a point where I couldn't afford. That same apartment now is $2300/mo. I've gotten a 2.5% raise since then, on Wednesday.

It's also extremely expensive to live here, and wages don't keep up. I moved downtown in October 2016 for $1600/mo. I had to move because my rent went up to a point where I couldn't afford. That same apartment now is $2300/mo. I've gotten a 2.5% raise since then, on Wednesday.

Vancouver is also, statistically, the most expensive city in North America (only below Hong Kong and Sydney) to live in, by almost a factor of 2. The average home price is 17 times the average gross income here. I will never be able to own a home, despite working a good job.

So basically, for all these reasons, and several more that I'm not listing, I plan on moving away. Relatively soon. Stress at my job has gotten to the point where I've thought of walking into traffic just to avoid work for a couple days.

Finding another job may be extremely difficult, but frankly at this point, I don't really care. It's not worth my happiness. I'll be moving east for sure, just not sure how far, and if south or not (keep in mind, Toronto is still south).

Another complaint about my job is that they overpromise. I moved where I did because I was told our office was moving and it was a sure thing. It never happened and now I was told it won't ever happen.

I was also told of opportunities in Toronto, Chicago, and Austin, all of which I'd be extremely interested in going to, but when I said I was interested, nothing else was ever said about those opportunities. It's just frustrating having the rug pulled out from under you.

tl;dr on thread: Job is stressful, leaving after SGDQ. No opportunity for advancement, long hours, promising things and taking them away. City is too difficult to live in, expensive as hell and wage doesn't match even CLOSE to inflation.
